evidence_at_a_glance.population: 4,046 patients with HER2-positive operable breast cancer
evidence_at_a_glance.applicability: Supports adding trastuzumab to the whole adjuvant strategy. Trial taxane schedules differed; not an isolated estimate for maintenance alone or preoperative response.
evidence_at_a_glance.qualitative_result: Do not attribute the whole strategy benefit solely to continuation after paclitaxel.
evidence_at_a_glance.harms: Cardiac toxicity is a key trade-off, particularly after anthracyclines; surveillance continues after chemotherapy.
limitations: Historical adjuvant population before contemporary dualHER2 and response-adapted postoperative options.
No concurrent AC/trastuzumab benefit is inferred.

treatment_rationale.summary: This sequence combines chemotherapy with trastuzumab because the cancer is HER2-positive. AC comes first; trastuzumab starts with paclitaxel and continues after chemotherapy. Receptor testing, recurrence risk, heart health and other HER2 options determine whether this is the right sequence.
treatment_rationale.setting: HER2-positive neoadjuvant or adjuvant high-risk breast cancer
treatment_rationale.line: Perioperative treatment for the stated early-breast indication; not a metastatic line. Confirm whether before or after surgery.
factors: Confirm histology, stage, tumour size/nodes, grade and HR/HER2 results.
Consider fitness, comorbidity, heart health, prior treatment and individual preferences.
Where indicated, MDT interpretation of a validated genomic assay may inform whether chemotherapy is worthwhile; no automated score threshold is applied.
alternatives: Discuss suitable endocrine/HER2-directed or other chemotherapy approaches for the actual biomarker and treatment setting.
Compare toxicity, treatment burden and evidence applicability; do not rank separate trials by their arm survival rates.
treatment_rationale.limitations: NCCP regimen availability is not proof that it is the preferred contemporary choice for every patient. Current Irish access and MDT selection require confirmation.

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Four AC cycles 21 days apart, then 12 weekly paclitaxel doses with weekly trastuzumab. Continue trastuzumab to complete one year total, without overlapping it with AC.

practical_workflow: Blood tests, relevant cardiac assessment, medicines review, fertility discussion and the consent conversation come first.

A cannula, PICC or implanted port may be used. If a port is chosen, a trained team inserts it in a separate procedure with local anaesthetic and sometimes sedation; the team explains fasting, blood-thinner and wound instructions.
Staff check the line, give prescribed premedicines and treatment, and observe for reactions. Tell them immediately about burning, pain, rash or breathlessness.
This regimen does not routinely need a take-home infusion pump. Staff disconnect the infusion; a port is de-accessed when appropriate. Keep line-care and next-visit instructions.
observation_and_access: The line team explains placement, dressing care and when normal activities can resume. A port is accessed with a special needle during treatment. Removal of the implanted device is a separate planned procedure when no longer needed; do not remove or adjust it yourself.

A PICC usually needs regular dressing and flushing appointments even between treatments. Fever, redness, swelling, pain, leakage or damage requires prompt advice. Your hospital supplies the exact care instructions.
First visits can take longer because of loading doses, premedicines and observation. Ask the unit about expected time, transport and any escort needed after sedation or line insertion.

Weekly taxane visits become less frequent if HER2 continuation switches to every three weeks. Infusion and observation times differ by drug and first versus later doses; the unit confirms the full visit duration, including blood review and preparation.
